$comment: Scoring methodology configuration. Bump 'version' whenever anything here changes:
it is hashed into configVersion, which is part of every cache key, so a weight change
correctly invalidates previously cached scores instead of serving stale numbers.
Weights are judgement calls, not facts. That is exactly why the aggregation mode is
switchable and why SensitivityAnalyzer resamples these weights to report whether a
ranking is robust or an artefact of how they were set.
$scaleComment: Metrics are normalized within an airport's FAA hub-class cohort, so a raw score measures
INTENSITY relative to peers, not the size of the opportunity. Without this adjustment a
best-in-class nonhub outranks a very good mega-hub — Bangor placed above Boston Logan as a
terminal expansion candidate, which is not a defensible answer for an investor.
The tilt is LOGARITHMIC on purpose. Weighting linearly by passengers would turn the ranking
into a size league table and throw away everything the pillars measure.
Switchable, like the aggregation mode, because 'how much does deal size matter' is a
strategic choice rather than a fact about the data.
$universeComment: Which airports count as candidates. The snapshot holds every airport BTS reports, including
general-aviation fields that logged a few charter passengers. Ranking the Atlanta metro
returned Gwinnett County (12 annual passengers) and Lee Gilmer (7) next to Hartsfield-Jackson.
2,500 is the FAA commercial-service threshold. Kept deliberately low: the point is to exclude
noise, not to pre-judge which small airports are interesting. Callers can override it.
$sensitivityComment: The weights below are judgement calls, not facts. Sensitivity analysis resamples them and
re-ranks, so the agent can distinguish a real finding from an artefact of how they were set.
On the first live New England run, three airports landed within 0.1 points and were printed
as ranks 2/3/4 — an ordering the data does not support.
weightSpread is a log-normal sigma: 0.35 means a typical draw moves a weight by about 40%,
and halving is exactly as likely as doubling.
seed is fixed so the same question always returns the same robustness figure.

terminal.label: Terminal expansion
terminal.description: Gates, holdrooms, concessions and international facilities. Weighted toward passenger throughput per gate, aircraft upgauging and high-yield traffic mix rather than runway queueing.

airfield.label: Airfield expansion
airfield.description: Runways, taxiways and apron. Weighted toward queueing delay, system-cause congestion and peak-hour saturation rather than terminal throughput.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: No assumption about which kind of capital project is on the table. Every metric carries its registry default weight.
